title: Chicken or Turkey with Noodles, No Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey with noodles, no sauce is a simple dish consisting of boiled noodles and tender white poultry meat, steamed or baked without added sauces. It is rich in protein, provides carbohydrates from the noodles, and contains a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is often served in school cafeterias and diet plans because it is easy to digest.
Noodles used can be wheat, rice or buckwheat, allowing variation of the glycemic index.
Chicken and turkey are among the most affordable meats, available fresh or frozen.
Lack of sauce makes the meal low‑calorie, suitable for weight management.
In some cultures the dish is finished with a sprinkle of herbs or a squeeze of lemon for flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Poultry meat contains all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Skinless chicken or turkey is very low in saturated fats, supporting heart health.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: Noodles provide a quick source of energy, especially useful after exercise.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is high in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, essential for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may develop an allergy to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Gluten in noodles
items.content: Traditional wheat noodles contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the noodles are pre‑salted, the dish may have a higher sodium level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally topping with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a drizzle of olive oil. It pairs well with vegetable sides such as broccoli or carrots.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked noodles and boiled poultry in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months.
